exact_changes.text: Here \(h^{\mathrm r}(z)=h(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\) and \(h^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\); \(\mathcal R^{-1}\) is the inverse real Euclidean Riesz isometry. Intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary stereographic smooth structure on \(S_n\).
Here \(W^{\mathrm r}(z)=W(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\) and \(W^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\). Intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary stereographic smooth structure on \(S_n\).

The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(g:S_n\to\mathbb R\), define \(g^{\mathrm r}(z)=g(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(g^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\nabla_S^{\mathrm{tot}}g(u)=P_u\mathcal R^{-1}(D_{\mathrm{tot}}g^{\mathrm r}(u))\). Here \(P_uv=v-\langle u,v\rangle u\), \(\mathcal R^{-1}\) is the inverse real Euclidean Riesz isometry, and \(D_{\mathrm{tot}}\) is the ordinary Fréchet derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Joint intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.

The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(G:S_n\to E_n\), define \(G^{\mathrm r}(z)=G(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(G^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\operatorname{div}_S^{\mathrm{tot}}G(u)=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)}\operatorname{deriv}_{\mathrm{tot}}[t\mapsto(G^{\mathrm r}(u+t e_j))_j](0)\). Here \(e_j\) is the standard Euclidean coordinate vector, and each total scalar derivative is the ordinary derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Pointwise tangency means \(V_i(x)\perp x_i\) for every \(i,x\); joint C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.
